content.overview: A late suit, appeal or application is dismissed even if the defendant never pleaded limitation.
content.study: The Court must notice limitation. The Schedule gives the period. Sections 4 to 24 are the only softening tools. A special law may oust this Act under section 29.

learningObjectives: Apply the provision to a limitation calculation or factual problem.
Distinguish the provision from related limitation rules.
enhancement.definition: Section 3 makes a prescribed limitation period a statutory bar: subject to the Act's scheme, a suit, appeal or application instituted after the prescribed period must be dismissed even if limitation is not set up as a defence.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Limitation is a statutory bar that the court must apply when the proceeding is instituted beyond the prescribed period, subject to the Act's computation and exclusion provisions.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Limitation Act, 1963, Section 3 read with the Schedule and Sections 4–24; special or local laws may modify the scheme through Section 29(2).
essentialIngredients: Identify the proceeding as a suit, appeal or application covered by Section 3.
Identify the prescribed period from the Schedule or applicable special/local law.
Compute the period using applicable Sections 4–24 and any valid exclusion.
Compare the filing date with the expiry date.
Apply the statutory bar unless the proceeding is within time after the applicable computation rules.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 3 is the central bar provision. It does not itself supply every limitation period; the period generally comes from the Schedule or an applicable special/local statute. A sound analysis therefore begins with the prescribed Article, identifies the starting point, applies relevant computation or exclusion provisions, and only then asks whether the proceeding is barred. Section 29(2) is important where another statute prescribes a different period.
examples: If the applicable Schedule article gives a three-year period and the cause accrued on a stated date, the court must calculate the period under the Act and determine whether the proceeding was instituted before expiry; if it was late, Section 3 requires dismissal subject to the Act's exceptions and computation rules.
enhancement.distinctions: Section 3 creates the bar; the Schedule generally supplies the period; Sections 4–24 contain computation, exclusion and extension mechanisms.
enhancement.problemApplication: Identify the cause of action, the relevant Schedule Article, the starting date, all applicable exclusions or extensions, and the filing date. Then conclude whether Section 3 bars the proceeding.
examAnswerStructure: Identify the prescribed period and triggering event
Conclude whether the proceeding is within time or what relief is available
